artists.biography:
The Sundays were an English alternative rock band. The band formed in the late 1980s and released three albums in the 1990s.

The band's beginnings came with the meeting of Harriet Wheeler and guitarist David Gavurin at university. Wheeler had played gigs with 'Cruel Shoes' an early incarnation of the band Jim Jiminee. The duo soon augmented the band with bassist Paul Brindley and drummer Patrick Hannan.

The Sundays secured a recording contract with Rough Trade Records. Their debut single was "Can't Be Sure". Their first album, Reading, Writing, and Arithmetic was released in 1990, along with their next single "Here's Where the Story Ends". The album was a UK Top 5 hit.

With Rough Trade's financial troubles and the band's decision to manage themselves, The Sundays' next single, "Goodbye", did not emerge until 1992. Their next album, Blind, arrived the same year, reaching the UK Top 15. The "Goodbye" B-side, a cover of The Rolling Stones' "Wild Horses", also appeared on the US release of Blind and on the soundtrack for the popular television series Buffy the Vampire Slayer. The band toured in support of these recordings.

In 1997 their third album, Static & Silence was followed by the release of their most successful single to date, "Summertime", which made the UK Top 15. The album itself reached the UK Top 10. However, the band has been on a lengthy hiatus since those releases, with Wheeler and Gavurin focusing on raising their two children.

perplexity.description:
Reading, Writing and Arithmetic is the debut studio album by English alternative rock band The Sundays, released in January 1990. The album's title references the band's hometown of Reading, Berkshire, rather than the educational concept. Arriving during the late 1980s alternative rock surge, the record showcases a delicate, introspective sound characterized by ethereal vocals and understated instrumentation that distinguished the band from the louder, more aggressive acts of their era.

The album established The Sundays' signature aesthetic—a blend of indie rock sensibility with pop accessibility and melancholic atmosphere. Standout tracks including "Here's Where the Story Ends" and "Can't Be Sure" demonstrated the band's gift for crafting memorable, emotionally resonant songs. Despite the band's limited material at the time and stated lack of commercial ambition, the album resonated with listeners and critics alike, becoming one of the most significant debut albums of the 1990s.

While The Sundays released two subsequent albums, Reading, Writing and Arithmetic remains their most celebrated work and the high point of their career. The record has endured as a touchstone of early 1990s alternative rock, maintaining its appeal decades after release. Though some critics noted the album's occasionally precious qualities, its sweet, beguiling character and fresh production have ensured its lasting influence on the alternative rock landscape.
